title: Palindrome Gate
story: The temple gate opens only to words that read the same both ways. Spaces and capitals do not count.
goal: Read a phrase. Print yes if it is a palindrome (ignoring spaces and case), otherwise no.

tests.label: A man a plan a canal Panama
stdin: A man a plan a canal Panama

hints: First clean the text: remove spaces and lowercase it. Then compare it with its reverse.

text = input()
clean = text.replace(" ", "").lower()
print("yes" if clean == clean[::-1] else "no")
socratic: What should you remove before comparing?
How do you get the reverse of a string?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the key idea in “Palindrome Gate”?
solution:
text = input()
clean = text.replace(" ", "").lower()
print("yes" if clean == clean[::-1] else "no")
